The Defense Intelligence Agency said Iran has used GPS jamming and other electronic warfare capabilities to disrupt U.S. space operations during Operation Epic Fury.
Iran also reportedly acquired Chinese satellite imagery to improve military targeting, while Russia has helped launch Iranian satellites.
Iran operates around a dozen satellites, but analysts question U.S. claims of space superiority, citing Tehran's continued jamming capabilities.
Source: Axios

Israeli intelligence detected a series of unusual Hamas activities in the hours before the October 7 attack, including senior commanders moving underground, Mohammed Deif preparing an emergency bunker, rocket launch sites being readied and anti-tank systems being tested, according to Kan News.
The warning signs began accumulating around 11:30 p.m., when intelligence officials identified unusual movements among senior Hamas figures. By midnight, commanders had been informed that Deif might have moved to an emergency facility. At 1:46 a.m., the office of Israel’s military chief was alerted, and less than an hour later, intelligence indicated that Hamas was preparing rocket launch sites.
Despite the mounting evidence, Israeli military officials largely interpreted the developments as routine activity or preparations for an exercise, failing to recognize that Hamas was preparing to launch a major assault just hours later.

🇾🇪🇸🇦 Houthis hold all the cards as Saudis seek exit ramp from Yemen 
Saudi Arabia approached Yemen’s Houthis pursuing a negotiated end to hostilities, with the movement proposing $51 billion in compensation and official recognition of Houthi rule as conditions for a settlement, The Wall Street Journal reports, citing people familiar with the discussions.
The Houthis argue that the money would compensate for years of Saudi airstrikes and blockade measures. More than a decade after Riyadh intervened in Yemen, the movement is now negotiating from a position of greater military strength. Not only have Houthi forces reportedly advanced to within 80 kilometers of Aden and consolidated their position near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, but missile and drone strikes also continue to target Saudi oil facilities and airports.
Riyadh’s options are narrowing as airstrikes fail to stop the Houthis and a ground offensive risks heavy losses. The UAE has withdrawn, Pakistan refuses to join any strikes, and Egypt offers only defensive support.

Iran will respond to any renewed military aggression with strikes extending beyond the location of the initial attack, Hamidreza Moqadamfar, adviser to the IRGC commander, warned.
💬 «Our responses will no longer be proportionate or commensurate; we will set their assets ablaze — beyond the point of attack, and regardless of time or location,» he said, outlining Iran’s new military doctrine.
Moqadamfar also warned that attacks on Iranian commanders would bring retaliation against enemy military and political leaders.
Speaking on the anniversary of the 1979 US embassy takeover in Tehran, he claimed that American military power in the region had suffered major setbacks, citing the downing of 56 advanced US drones.
The adviser also linked Republicans’ midterm defeat to the economic fallout from the Iran war, describing the election as «a major referendum against Trump’s policies» in which Iran «played a key role.»

🇺🇸🇮🇷US Treasury issues new Iran-linked sanctions, continuing escalatory actions
Individuals and companies in India and Turkey have been hit with US economic sanctions as part of President Donald Trump’s “Operation Economic Outcast” for allegedly aiding Iran, just a day after Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections.
💬 “We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, and two other Indian citizens allegedly defrauded maritime regulatory authorities in several countries, including Guyana, Eswatini and Laos, by claiming to represent them and issuing flags and certifications. This allowed vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies to evade international restrictions and continue operating, according to the US Treasury.
The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for its support of Iran’s aviation sector.
